method.name: bounded triangular Monte Carlo with Gaussian copula
method.draw_procedure: Generate N x 4 standard normals, apply the lower Cholesky factor, transform the first two columns through the scalar standard-normal CDF, and replace the last two columns with independent Generator.random uniforms. Apply analytic inverse triangular CDFs.
method.validity: Retain only finite draws inside declared inclusive bounds with revenue growth > -1, nonnegative EBIT margin, and WACC > terminal g. n_rejected counts invalid generated paths.
method.terminal_value: FY5 FCFF * (1 + terminal_growth) / (path WACC - terminal_growth), discounted by path FY5 discount factor

revenue_growth.unit: decimal annual revenue growth, constant within a path

ebit_margin.unit: decimal EBIT / revenue, constant within a path

reinvestment_intensity.unit: decimal of annual revenue; CapEx plus NWC increase minus D&A; positive consumes cash

dependence.matrix_interpretation: Pearson correlation of pre-copula Gaussian scores, not an exact target for realized triangular Pearson correlations
dependence.explanation: Revenue growth and EBIT margin have positively correlated Gaussian scores (0.35), representing shared subscription/advertising execution. Reinvestment intensity and WACC have independent scores; aggregate history cannot identify these causal relationships.

percentile_convention: linear: sort N values; h=(N-1)q; value=x[floor(h)]+(h-floor(h))*(x[ceil(h)]-x[floor(h)]); zero-based indices
limitations: The distribution is conditional on analyst-selected triangular bounds and a Gaussian copula; it is not a stock-price forecast or a market consensus estimate.
Four fiscal-year growth observations and five margin observations cannot identify joint operating dynamics; the 0.35 growth/margin score correlation is an open assumption.
Membership, churn/retention, price, advertising ARPU, content cash spend, and content amortization are not separately available in the frozen history.
Constant path growth, margin, and reinvestment intensity omit competitive responses, content cycles, annual state transitions, and stochastic terminal growth.
Reinvestment is a reduced-form cash-flow proxy; it does not separately reconstruct content-asset investment. SBC remains an operating cost and is not added back.
Tax, cash/investments, gross debt, and shares are fixed at their disclosed model assumptions; no financing feedback or repurchase-price model is simulated.
Terminal value is highly sensitive to the WACC-g spread. The simulation terminal growth is fixed at the model assumption, 3%, below every sampled WACC.
